Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

Original source context
import java.util.*;
class Main { 
    public static int matchingASCIIDigits(int n, int arr[], String s)
    {
        int count = 0;
        HashSet<Integer> hs = new HashSet<>();
        for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
        {
            hs.add(arr[i]);
        }
        
        int k = s.length();
        for(int i=0;i<k;i++)
        {
            int ascii = s.charAt(i);
            int ones = ascii % 10;
            int tens = ascii / 10;
            if (hs.contains(ones) || hs.contains(tens))
            {
                count++;
            }
        }
        return count;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        int n = 6;
        int arr[] = {1,6,4,3,6,5};
        String s = "ABCDEF";
        System.out.println(matchingASCIIDigits(n, arr, s));
    }
}
